005package org.wpilib.command3.button;
006
007import org.wpilib.command3.Scheduler;
008import org.wpilib.command3.Trigger;
009import org.wpilib.driverstation.DriverStation;
010import org.wpilib.driverstation.Joystick;
011import org.wpilib.event.EventLoop;
012
013/**
014 * A version of {@link Joystick} with {@link Trigger} factories for command-based.
015 *
016 * @see Joystick
017 */
018public class CommandJoystick {
019  private final CommandGenericHID m_hid;
020  private final Joystick m_joystick;
021
022  /**
023   * Construct an instance of a controller.
024   *
025   * @param port The port index on the Driver Station that the controller is plugged into.
026   */
027  public CommandJoystick(int port) {
028    this(Scheduler.getDefault(), port);
029  }
030
031  /**
032   * Construct an instance of a controller.
033   *
034   * @param scheduler The scheduler that should execute the triggered commands.
035   * @param port The port index on the Driver Station that the controller is plugged into.
036   */
037  public CommandJoystick(Scheduler scheduler, int port) {
038    m_hid = CommandGenericHID.getCommandGenericHID(scheduler, port);
039    m_joystick = new Joystick(DriverStation.getGenericHID(port));
040  }
041
042  /**
043   * Get the underlying CommandGenericHID object.
044   *
045   * @return the wrapped CommandGenericHID object
046   */
047  public CommandGenericHID getHID() {
048    return m_hid;
049  }
050
051  /**
052   * Get the underlying Joystick object.
053   *
054   * @return the wrapped Joystick object
055   */
056  public Joystick getJoystick() {
057    return m_joystick;
058  }
059
060  /**
061   * Constructs an event instance around the trigger button's digital signal.
062   *
063   * @return an event instance representing the trigger button's digital signal attached to the
064   *     {@link Scheduler#getDefaultEventLoop() default scheduler button loop}.
065   * @see #trigger(EventLoop)
066   */
067  public Trigger trigger() {
068    return trigger(m_hid.getScheduler().getDefaultEventLoop());
069  }
070
071  /**
072   * Constructs an event instance around the trigger button's digital signal.
073   *
074   * @param loop the event loop instance to attach the event to.
075   * @return an event instance representing the trigger button's digital signal attached to the
076   *     given loop.
077   */
078  public Trigger trigger(EventLoop loop) {
079    return m_hid.button(Joystick.ButtonType.TRIGGER.value, loop);
080  }
081
082  /**
083   * Constructs an event instance around the top button's digital signal.
084   *
085   * @return an event instance representing the top button's digital signal attached to the {@link
086   *     Scheduler#getDefaultEventLoop() default scheduler button loop}.
087   * @see #top(EventLoop)
088   */
089  public Trigger top() {
090    return top(m_hid.getScheduler().getDefaultEventLoop());
091  }
092
093  /**
094   * Constructs an event instance around the top button's digital signal.
095   *
096   * @param loop the event loop instance to attach the event to.
097   * @return an event instance representing the top button's digital signal attached to the given
098   *     loop.
099   */
100  public Trigger top(EventLoop loop) {
101    return m_hid.button(Joystick.ButtonType.TOP.value, loop);
102  }
103
104  /**
105   * Set the channel associated with the X axis.
106   *
107   * @param channel The channel to set the axis to.
108   */
109  public void setXChannel(int channel) {
110    m_joystick.setXChannel(channel);
111  }
112
113  /**
114   * Set the channel associated with the Y axis.
115   *
116   * @param channel The channel to set the axis to.
117   */
118  public void setYChannel(int channel) {
119    m_joystick.setYChannel(channel);
120  }
121
122  /**
123   * Set the channel associated with the Z axis.
124   *
125   * @param channel The channel to set the axis to.
126   */
127  public void setZChannel(int channel) {
128    m_joystick.setZChannel(channel);
129  }
130
131  /**
132   * Set the channel associated with the throttle axis.
133   *
134   * @param channel The channel to set the axis to.
135   */
136  public void setThrottleChannel(int channel) {
137    m_joystick.setThrottleChannel(channel);
138  }
139
140  /**
141   * Set the channel associated with the twist axis.
142   *
143   * @param channel The channel to set the axis to.
144   */
145  public void setTwistChannel(int channel) {
146    m_joystick.setTwistChannel(channel);
147  }
148
149  /**
150   * Get the channel currently associated with the X axis.
151   *
152   * @return The channel for the axis.
153   */
154  public int getXChannel() {
155    return m_joystick.getXChannel();
156  }
157
158  /**
159   * Get the channel currently associated with the Y axis.
160   *
161   * @return The channel for the axis.
162   */
163  public int getYChannel() {
164    return m_joystick.getYChannel();
165  }
166
167  /**
168   * Get the channel currently associated with the Z axis.
169   *
170   * @return The channel for the axis.
171   */
172  public int getZChannel() {
173    return m_joystick.getZChannel();
174  }
175
176  /**
177   * Get the channel currently associated with the twist axis.
178   *
179   * @return The channel for the axis.
180   */
181  public int getTwistChannel() {
182    return m_joystick.getTwistChannel();
183  }
184
185  /**
186   * Get the channel currently associated with the throttle axis.
187   *
188   * @return The channel for the axis.
189   */
190  public int getThrottleChannel() {
191    return m_joystick.getThrottleChannel();
192  }
193
194  /**
195   * Get the x position of the HID.
196   *
197   * <p>This depends on the mapping of the joystick connected to the current port. On most
198   * joysticks, positive is to the right.
199   *
200   * @return the x position
201   */
202  public double getX() {
203    return m_joystick.getX();
204  }
205
206  /**
207   * Get the y position of the HID.
208   *
209   * <p>This depends on the mapping of the joystick connected to the current port. On most
210   * joysticks, positive is to the back.
211   *
212   * @return the y position
213   */
214  public double getY() {
215    return m_joystick.getY();
216  }
217
218  /**
219   * Get the z position of the HID.
220   *
221   * @return the z position
222   */
223  public double getZ() {
224    return m_joystick.getZ();
225  }
226
227  /**
228   * Get the twist value of the current joystick. This depends on the mapping of the joystick
229   * connected to the current port.
230   *
231   * @return The Twist value of the joystick.
232   */
233  public double getTwist() {
234    return m_joystick.getTwist();
235  }
236
237  /**
238   * Get the throttle value of the current joystick. This depends on the mapping of the joystick
239   * connected to the current port.
240   *
241   * @return The Throttle value of the joystick.
242   */
243  public double getThrottle() {
244    return m_joystick.getThrottle();
245  }
246
247  /**
248   * Get the magnitude of the vector formed by the joystick's current position relative to its
249   * origin.
250   *
251   * @return The magnitude of the direction vector
252   */
253  public double getMagnitude() {
254    return m_joystick.getMagnitude();
255  }
256
257  /**
258   * Get the direction of the vector formed by the joystick and its origin in radians. 0 is forward
259   * and clockwise is positive. (Straight right is π/2.)
260   *
261   * @return The direction of the vector in radians
262   */
263  public double getDirectionRadians() {
264    // https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/basic-programming/coordinate-system.html#joystick-and-controller-coordinate-system
265    // A positive rotation around the X axis moves the joystick right, and a
266    // positive rotation around the Y axis moves the joystick backward. When
267    // treating them as translations, 0 radians is measured from the right
268    // direction, and angle increases clockwise.
269    //
270    // It's rotated 90 degrees CCW (y is negated and the arguments are reversed)
271    // so that 0 radians is forward.
272    return m_joystick.getDirectionRadians();
273  }
274
275  /**
276   * Get the direction of the vector formed by the joystick and its origin in degrees. 0 is forward
277   * and clockwise is positive. (Straight right is 90.)
278   *
279   * @return The direction of the vector in degrees
280   */
281  public double getDirectionDegrees() {
282    return m_joystick.getDirectionDegrees();
283  }
284}
